questions.question: Which among the following is a river that originates in the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandovi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Mandovi River-**

__
 
• It originates from a cluster of 30 springs at Bhimgad in the **Western Ghats** in the Belagavi district of **Karnataka**.
 
• The river has a total catchment area of 2032 sq km, of which 1580 sq km lies in Goa.
 
• **Panaji** is situated on the banks of the river Mandovi.
 
• **Dudhsagar Falls **in Goa are also formed by this river.
 
• The river passes through Karnataka and Goa before it empties into the **Arabian Sea.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Narmada River-**

 
• Narmada originates from **Amarkantak** in the Anupur district of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• Narmada is the longest river in MP and the **5th largest river** in the country.
 
• Narmada is also the largest **west**-flowing river in India.
 
• The total length of Narmada is **1312 km **and its total length in Madhya Pradesh is **1077 km.**
 
• Narmada does not form a delta, it forms an **estuary.**

**Luni River-**

 
• Luni River originates from Nag Pahar or **Naga hills** in the **Ajmer** district of **Rajasthan**.
 
• Luni originates in the Pushkar valley of the **Aravalli Range,** near Ajmer, and passes through the southeastern portion of the Thar Desert.
 
• It ends in the marshy lands of **Rann of** **Kutch** in **Gujarat**.
 
• **Jaswant Sagar Dam** was built in **1892** by Maharaja Jaswant Singh. It is one of the largest artificial lakes in India.

**Banas River-**

 
• Banas River originates from Khamnor Hills of **Aravalli Range,** near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, **Rajasthan**.
 
• Banas River is a tributary of the **Chambal River** and it is approximately **512** kilometers in length.
 
• This river is also called** ‘Van Ki Asha‘.**

questions.question: Among the following, in which material the speed of sound is highest? (at 25°C)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Out of the following, the speed of sound is maximum in **Aluminium**.
 
• Speed of sound in Aluminium at 25 deg Celsius is around **6420 m/s.**
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** and needs a material medium for its propagation. It **cannot travel** through a **vacuum**.
 
• Sound travels at different speeds depending on what it is traveling through. 
 
• Of the three mediums **(gas, liquid, and solid)** sound waves travel the slowest through gases, faster through liquids, and fastest through solids. 
 
• **Temperature also affects the speed of sound.**
 
• For Example, at 0º Celcius, sound travels through air at 331 meters per second, but, at 20ºC, at room temperature, sound travels at 343 meters per second.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to view pages and navigate the World Wide Web?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Web Browser.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Web Browser is a **software application** used to access information on the **WWW (World Wide Web).**
 
• When a user requests some information, the web browser fetches the data from a web server and then displays the webpage on the user’s screen. 
 
• Visiting any website can be done using a web browser. When a **URL (Uniform Resource Locator)** is entered in a browser, the web server takes us to that website.
 
• Example of Web Browser- **Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera Mini, Microsoft edge, etc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Hyperlink-**

 
• A hyperlink is a text or an icon that you can click on to get to another website.
 
• Hyperlinks are found on virtually every webpage to help navigate readers to other pages and websites.
 
• The default formatting for a hyperlink on a webpage or in a document is **blue**, **underlined text**.

**World Wide Web-**

 
• The **World Wide Web (WWW)** is a network of online content that is formatted in **HTML (Hypertext Markup Language)** and accessed via **HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol).**
 
• **Tim Berners Lee** invented the World Wide Web in **1989**.

**Joystick-**

 
• A joystick is an **input device** that can be used for controlling the movement of the cursor or a pointer in a computer device.
 
• A joystick is also known as the **control column.**
 
• The joystick is used for **gaming** purposes.

questions.question: Which among the following forts was principal capital of Qutb Shahi dynasty in Hyderabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golconda Fort.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Golconda Fort:-​**

 
 
• The Golconda Fort was built by the Qutubshahi of the Qutub Shahi Dynasty.
 
• Golconda Fort is a fortified citadel.
 
• It was the capital city of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
 
• It is located in Hyderabad, Telangana. 
 
• It was originally known as Mankal and built on a hilltop in 1143.
 
• It has thick walls and tall heavy gates with sharp iron spokes.
 
• In some places, a part of the wall comes out in a round shape.
 
• These are called bastions *(Burj)*.
 
• These bastions have small holes in them to attack enemies while being hidden.
 
• These are even higher than the wall.
 
• The outer wall of this fort has 87 bastions.
 
• The Golconda Fort was made strong and big to protect it from any outside enemy attack.
 
• In 1200, this fort was made of mud and different rulers lived here.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Red Fort (Lal Qila):- 

 
 
• It is a monument built in 1638 that rises 33 meters (108 ft) above Old Delhi.
 
• It was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the mid-17th century. The fort is located in what is now the center of Delhi, India.
 
• Red Fort massive, 2.5-km-long enclosing walls are made of red sandstone and that's where the monument got its name from.
 
• A few parts of the fort are also made of red stone while the remaining structure is built using marble.
 
 
 
• **Rajgad Fort:-****​**
 
 
• ​​It is a fort situated in the Pune district of Maharastra.
 
• It was also known as Murumdev.
 
• It served as the capital of the Maratha Empire under the rule of Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 
 
 
• **Chiktan Fort:-**
 
 
• **​**Chiktan Fort is **located in Chiktan village of Kargil district** by the river Indus.
 
• The fort was built in the 16th century and had nine stories.
 
• Balti craftsmen constructed the castle in the 16th century which served as a royal residence for centuries.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a type of Right to freedom in the Indian constitution?

options.text: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
Protection of life and personal liberty
Protection in respect of conviction for offences.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**offences for armed assembly.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Right to Freedom

 
 
• The objective of the Indian Constitution is to ensure freedom of thought, expression, belief, religion, and worship. Therefore, the Right to Freedom has been mentioned in the Indian Constitution from Articles 19 to 22.
 
• In these, provisions have been given keeping in mind all the sections of the people of the country, so that any person can do any work of his mind, but that work should not be illegal and unconstitutional, nor should that work be done by any other person such that the fundamental rights should be violated.
 
• Article 19 of the Indian Constitution is most important in this regard. Article 19 of the Indian Constitution at present describes only 6 freedoms for the citizens of the country, which are as follows
 
 
• Freedom of thought and expression
 
• Freedom of arms and peaceful assembly.
 
• Community and freedom of association
 
• Freedom of travel
 
• Freedom of residence
 
• Freedom of trade (Hence option 1 is correct)
 
 
 
• Article 20 offers protection in respect of conviction for offences. **(Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• Article 21 offers protection of life and personal liberty. **(Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• Article 22 offers protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

questions.question: International Day for the preservation of the Ozone layer is observed on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **September 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Ozone Layer:-**

 
 
• International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer or World Ozone Day is observed on September 16, every year.
 
• It is celebrated **to spread awareness among people about the depletion of the Ozone Layer **and** search for possible solutions to preserve it.**
 
• On December 19, 1994, the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed September 16 the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.
 
• On September 16, 1987, the United Nations and 45 other countries signed the Montreal Protocol, on substances that deplete the Ozone layer.
 
• The purpose of the Montreal Protocol is to protect the Ozone layer by reducing the production of substances that are supposed to be responsible for Ozone layer depletion.
 
• In 1985, the world’s governments adopted the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following planets is considered as Earth’s twin planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus**:-

 
 
• Venus is sometimes called Earth's twin because Venus and Earth are almost the same size, have about the same mass (they weigh about the same), and have a very similar composition (are made of the same material).
 
• They are also neighboring planets.
 
• However, Venus and Earth are also very different.
 
• Venus has an atmosphere that is about 100 times thicker than Earth's and has surface temperatures that are extremely hot.
 
• Venus does not have life or water oceans like Earth does.
 
• Venus also rotates backward compared to Earth and the other planets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neptune:-

 
 
• It was discovered on the basis of the law of gravitation.
 
• It is the farthest known planet from the Sun in the Solar System.
 
• Its revolution period is 164 years and the rotation period is 16 hours and 7 minutes.
 
• Neptune and Uranus are the only two planets discovered with the help of a telescope.
 
 
 
• **Uranus**:-
 
 
• It is the seventh planet from the Sun and has the third-largest diameter in our solar system.
 
• It was the first planet found with the aid of a telescope, Uranus was discovered in 1781 by astronomer William Herschel, although he originally thought it was either a comet or a star.
 
 
 
• **Mars:-****​**
 
 
• Mars is called Red Planet.
 
• It has two satellites - Phobos and Deimos.
 
• Mars is the fourth planet in the solar system.
 
• It is the second smallest planet in the solar system.
 
• In English Mars carries the name of the Roman God of War.

questions.question: Which animal's memorial was inaugurated in September 2022 at Kaziranga National Park in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rhinoceros**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhinoceros:- **

 
 
• ​​They are found in the **Indian subcontinent.**
 
• It is listed as **Vulnerable **on the IUCN Red List.
 
• **90% are found in Kaziranga National Park.**
 
• There are 2,640 rhinoceros in four protected areas in Assam.
 
• They are mainly found in Assam, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The one-horned rhinoceros (Indian rhinoceros) are the largest of the rhino species.
 
• The National Rhino Conservation Strategy was launched in the year 2019 for the conservation of big-horned rhinos.
 
• Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was launched in 2005, it is an ambitious effort to attain a wild population of at least 3,000 greater one-horned rhinos spread over seven protected areas in the Indian state of Assam by the year 2020.
 
 
 
• ** Kaziranga National Park:-**
 
 
• Kaziranga National Park’s 430 sq. km. area sprinkled with dense forests
 
• This is home to more than 2200 Indian one-horned rhinoceros, approximately 2/3rd of their total world population.
 
• It was formed in 1908 on the recommendation of Mary Curzon, the park is located on the edge of the Eastern Himalayan biodiversity hotspots – Golaghat and Nagaon districts.
 
• Kaziranga national park present in Assam is famous for conserving Rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicorns).
 
• It is basically a reserve of natural, semi-natural, or developed land that a sovereign state declares or owns.
 
• Kaziranga National Park is a national park in the Golaghat and Nagaon districts of the state of Assam, India.

questions.question: Which of the following base is found in lime water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium hydroxide**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium hydroxide:-**

 
 
• It is used to neutralize excess acidity.
 
• For example, lakes and soils are affected by acid rain.
 
• Calcium hydroxide dissolves in water to produce limewater, which is used to test carbon dioxide.
 
• The pH value of Calcium hydroxide is ranging from 9 to 11.5.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potassium hydroxide:-​**

 
 
• ​Potassium hydroxide is an inorganic compound with the components KOH and is generally referred to as caustic potash.
 
• KOH is noteworthy as the precursor to maximum smooth and liquid soaps, as well as numerous potassium-containing chemicals. 
 
• Even at high temperatures, solid KOH does not dehydrate without difficulty.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide:-​**
 
 
• It is a white-colored substance, slightly soluble in water.
 
• A suspension of Mg(OH)2 in water is called Milk of magnesia.
 
• It is used as an antacid, as a laxative, and for neutralizing acid wastewater.
 
• It is also used in the treatment of scalp dandruff.
 
 
 
• **Ammonium hydroxide:-​**
 
 
• The chemical formula for ammonium hydroxide is NH4OH.
 
• Ammonium hydroxide is a colorless liquid with a strong, pungent odor.
 
• It is made by dissolving ammonia gas in water, and the resulting solution contains around 30-35% ammonia by weight.

questions.question: Godaan is a novel written by Munshi Premchand, published in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1936.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Godaan is a **Hindi novel **written by **Munshi Premchand**, published in the year **1936.**
 
• It was first published in 1936 and is considered one of** Premchand's most renowned works.**
 
• Munshi Premchand, whose real name was** Dhanpat Rai Srivastava,** was** born on July 31, 1880, in Lamhi, near Varanasi.**
 
• His literary contributions earned him the title of** "Upanyas Samrat"** (Emperor of Novels).
 
• Some of his famous novels are** Nirmala, Rangbhoomi, Gaban, Kafan etc.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rangbhoomi**

 
 
• It was published in **1924** and is considered one of Munshi Premchand's significant works.
 
• This novel explores various social issues prevalent in Indian society during the **colonial era, such as corruption, exploitation, and the struggle for justice.**
 
• It revolves around the world of theatre, highlighting the challenges and complexities faced by artists, their conflicts, and their efforts to bring about social change through their art.
 
 
 
• **Gaban**
 
 
• It was published in **1931** and is considered one of Munshi Premchand's notable works.
 
• The novel delves into **themes of greed, social hypocrisy, and the consequences of materialism in Indian society.**
 
• The story revolves around Ramanath, the main character, who succumbs to his desires for wealth and social status. The novel follows his journey as he becomes entangled in a web of deceit and faces the consequences of his actions.
 
 
 
• **Kafan**
 
 
• It depicts the bleak and tragic life of a poor peasant named Gheesu and his son Madhav, who struggle with extreme poverty and societal indifference.
 
• The story explores **themes of poverty, social inequality, and the dehumanizing effects of a rigid caste system **prevalent in rural Indian society.
 
• "Kafan" serves as a sharp critique of the oppressive social conditions and the apathy of the privileged classes towards the** suffering of the poor.**
